items.notes: Developer screening is personnel vetting; the text itself points to PS-3 territory.
Broad AI governance program (inventory, risk, compliance, literacy) best fits the AI management system hub; parent organizational AI controls is also defensible.
Attack poisons training datasets via expiring URLs in the supply chain; fundamentally dataset poisoning, though supply-chain model poisoning is a near miss.
Primarily evasion of network filtering controls; DoS is a secondary effect, so network defense-in-depth fits better than DoS protection, but neither is clean.
Encrypting AI models at rest is fundamentally data-at-rest encryption; protection of technical AI information is a reasonable alternative.
Attack exploits cleartext traffic after SSL termination between edge and backend; end-to-end encryption of all communications is the counter, with inter-component protection close behind.
Technique covers both direct and indirect prompt injection, so the inference-threats parent is the honest fit; either child is defensible.
Reconnaissance scanning has no dedicated hub; network defense-in-depth detection is the nearest home.
Spans alignment training, prompt formatting/segregation, and I/O detection filters for prompt injection; I/O handling is the closest single hub.
Encoding tricks to bypass URL validation are input-validation bypass/injection; whitelist input validation is also defensible.
Routing/DNS manipulation (pharming) maps loosely to DNS integrity; broader than that hub but no better fit exists.
Unicode smuggling past filters is canonical injection-protection territory.
Adversarial training and robust distillation are named; adversarial training is the primary technique.
Rootkit installation is malware; only endpoint malware protection hub approximates it.
Non-network audio eavesdropping has no real hub; physical protection is the least-bad fit.
Input restoration is explicitly named under evasion attack input handling; AI input distortion also covers restoration-style transforms.
Attack pattern (firewall reconnaissance via ACK scan) has no direct hub; nearest is network-based attack detection/protection.
Rogue location resembling a legitimate resource is closest to domain/DNS integrity (typosquatting-like); no exact hub exists.
Attack exploits unprotected cached sensitive data; defense maps to protect-and-clear cached sensitive data.
Control covers both direct and indirect prompt injection, so the common parent fits better than either leaf.
Covers both training-data privacy inference and model extraction via the inference API; no single leaf covers both.
Buffer overflow from expanded input; memory-safe functions hub is the closest preventive home.
Harvesting data leaked through application events; nearest concept is preventing security disclosure, but fit is weak.
OS fingerprinting probe; no reconnaissance hub, nearest is network attack detection/protection.
Contingency-specific role training; contingency planning hub covers the domain, awareness training is the alternative.
PII quality operations fall under personal data handling management per its description.
Port scanning attack pattern; no dedicated reconnaissance hub.
SYN scan reconnaissance; same reasoning as other scan items.
Attack denies availability of name resolution by dropping DNS requests; sits between DNS service protection and DoS protection.
Reducing output fidelity to hinder model extraction matches obscuring confidence/output information in AI responses.
Attack exploits missing access control on sensitive files; fundamentally an authorization enforcement failure.
AitM attack succeeds because traffic is not TLS-protected; core countermeasure is encrypting all communications, with public WiFi as the typical vector.
Text spans software, data, and model supply chains for AI; parent hub fits better than any single leaf.
OS fingerprinting via ICMP error quoting has no precise hub; nearest is layered network defense limiting such responses.
Buffer overflow in MIME conversion routines; prevention is memory-safe functions, though the mail-parsing context is incidental.
Covers backdoor testing, leakage testing, adversarial influence, and drift monitoring; spans several leaf hubs so the assurance parent fits best.
Host discovery reconnaissance has no dedicated hub; closest is network defense-in-depth detection.
Code inclusion via local/remote file references aligns with LFI/RFI protection; blocking execution of untrusted logic is a defensible alternative.
General interaction-frequency limiting; authentication-specific cases would fall under restrict excessive authentication.
General information/records retention across the lifecycle; 268-272 is limited to personal data retention/deletion, so the broader data classification and handling parent is the better home.
Threat of LLMs disclosing sensitive data (PII, training data, proprietary info) through model output; inversion is mentioned only as a secondary consequence.
Improper handling of missing/undefined parameters is fundamentally an input validation weakness; whitelist validation of external HTTP input is the closest leaf.
Exponential data expansion is resource-exhaustion DoS; 163-518 covers only archive decompression bombs, a narrower special case.
Buffer overflow via binary resources; the memory-safe functions leaf is the preventive hub for this weakness class.
Primarily training data poisoning; augmentation data manipulation is mentioned as a variant, hence secondary.
Malicious payloads delivered in files via standard channels; malware scanning of untrusted files is the closest defensive hub, though the attack also spans file type validation and safe serving.
Cache poisoning spans DNS/ARP and application caches; the name resolution hub explicitly covers cache poisoning prevention, though the pattern is broader than DNS.
Rogue access point / Wi-Fi interception is squarely wireless link protection.
Exposure of sensitive info via derived metadata/search indices; no leaf fits well, so the Prevent security disclosure parent is the least-bad home.
Hardware fault injection is a physical/environmental attack on devices; no dedicated hub exists, physical & environment protection is closest though aimed at facilities.

Single-use action enforcement (vote once) is a business logic constraint; no hub covers uniqueness directly, so business logic limits is the closest fit, with sequence enforcement as a secondary candidate.
Threat technique covering collection of models, datasets, and telemetry; spans development-time leak, runtime leak, and exfiltration, so the parent model confidentiality hub is the safest home.
Attack pattern that disables security tooling to evade detection; taxonomy has no hub for protecting detective controls themselves, so Monitoring is the nearest concept.
Rainbow tables are defeated by salted hashing; the salted-and-hashed hub is the direct countermeasure home.
Time-based removal of data no longer needed matches training data retention management in the AI context; data minimization and personal-data retention classification are defensible alternatives.
Formal verification of adversarial robustness is a verification method against evasion attacks, fitting the testing-against-evasion hub despite its formal-methods flavor.
Validating generative output against security/content/privacy policy is broader than sensitive-output filtering; automated oversight with output filtering is the best fit.
OS fingerprinting probe via IP DF bit; no hub addresses reconnaissance or protocol-level information leakage, so network defense-in-depth is a weak nearest home.
Custom reimplementation of untrusted critical components is an architectural trust decision; no hub covers high-assurance custom development directly.
Weakness is sharing of high-privilege device unlock credentials across parties; shared privileged accounts hub fits best though the context is hardware credentials.
Network reconnaissance via traceroute; no dedicated hub, nearest is network defense-in-depth.
Validating index/offset input is fundamentally input validation; integer-overflow boundary checking is a partial near-miss since offsets feed buffer arithmetic.
Hardware attestation/measurement register tampering has no real home; binary integrity verification is the closest integrity-check concept.
Manipulation of the model's primary task via prompts at inference; text explicitly distinguishes it from indirect prompt injection, so the broader inference-time behavior-integrity hub fits best.
Cross-field consistency validation of structured input maps best to schema enforcement on structured data; general HTTP input whitelisting is a defensible alternative.
Memory exhaustion of the web service via oversized array declaration is a resource-exhaustion DoS attack.
Reconnaissance against time-based security algorithms (RNG seeding, time-based auth); nearest hub is proper secure-random generation, but the taxonomy has no clean home for this recon pattern.
Covers both model artifact integrity (safe formats, scanning) and training-data download verification; model supply chain is primary, data supply chain acceptable.
ICMP-based network reconnaissance; only the network defense-in-depth hub plausibly covers detection/blocking of such probes, but fit is loose.
Root cause cited is insufficient access controls on log files enabling injection/forgery/deletion; log access protection is primary, log injection protection acceptable.
Core dump exposure to unauthorized actors is sensitive diagnostic-data disclosure; no leaf hub directly covers dump files, so the disclosure-prevention parent is the safest home.
URL encoding abuse to bypass filters and subvert parameter meaning is fundamentally an injection/interpretation attack; uniform encoder/parser enforcement is the preventive-control alternative.
Nested-payload parser attacks aim at memory/CPU exhaustion (DoS); deserialization-prevention hubs address object instantiation rather than parser resource exhaustion.
Core content is manipulation of pre-training/fine-tuning/embedding data; model artifacts via shared repositories are secondary, making supply-chain poisoning acceptable.
Attack exploits missing client authentication in the channel; authenticating all external connections is the countermeasure hub.
Account enumeration via legitimate OS query functionality; taxonomy lacks a reconnaissance/account-enumeration hub, so general disclosure prevention is the least-bad fit.
Broad evasion-robustness training control spanning adversarial training, noise injection, and gradient masking; parent hub fits better than the adversarial-training-specific leaf.
Network reconnaissance attack pattern; no reconnaissance hub exists, so the layered network defense/detection hub is the nearest home.
Control restricts tool/action privileges when untrusted data enters context, matching model action privilege minimization; indirect prompt injection is the threat addressed.
Cryptanalysis of cellular encryption is a wireless-link confidentiality threat; weak-crypto hub is about sanctioned legacy use, not this attack surface.
Randomized smoothing is explicitly named in the AI Input distortion hub description.
Improper privilege management maps to least-privilege enforcement; broad CWE could also sit under strong authorization checking.
Bluetooth key negotiation attack is squarely a wireless link protection concern.
Model size reduction hub is scoped to backdoor mitigation, but this control uses small models to prevent memorization of training samples (privacy); no better hub exists.
Abuse of privileged features exposed to lower-privilege accounts reflects failure of least privilege; admin-functionality restriction is a plausible alternative.
Multi-modal sensor fusion is an ensemble-style architectural defense against single-point adversarial/physical attack.
OS fingerprinting is reconnaissance via information disclosure; the HTTP header hub explicitly names fingerprinting but is HTTP-scoped, so fit is imperfect.
Missing salt is the core weakness; the salted-and-hashed hub is also defensible.
Buffer overflow via symlink contents is fundamentally a memory-safety/bounds-checking failure.
Attack hinges on applications failing unsafely on corrupted input; integrity verification of files is a plausible alternative but no hub covers corrupted-file handling directly.
System-prompt guidelines steering model behavior toward safe outputs align with GenAI alignment; prompt segregation is a near-miss focused on input structure.
Broad improper access control weakness fits the strong authorization checking branch; least privilege is a defensible narrower leaf.
Dataset provenance tracking is squarely data supply chain management.
Attack pattern; the corresponding defensive concept is throttling/blocking brute-force authentication attempts.
Network reconnaissance/host discovery has no dedicated hub; nearest is network defense-in-depth including detection of network-based probing.
Component inventory is asset management; the only inventory leaf (863-521) is scoped to third-party software components and excludes hardware/firmware.
Port/OS scanning technique; no reconnaissance hub exists, closest is layered network defense/detection.
Data reconstruction via model inversion/membership inference on training data.
Ajax-based enumeration/footprinting; defensible as automation abuse detection or generic network defense, no true recon hub.
Stealth port scanning; mapped to network defense-in-depth for lack of a reconnaissance hub.
Fingerprinting defense maps best to preventing disclosure of technical information (versions, banners) in responses.
Economy of mechanism is a design-level architectural security principle; no dedicated hub exists.
Buffer overflow via oversized formatted strings; defense is memory-safe functions/boundary checking.
Checksum verification of AI artifacts fits model supply chain integrity; generic trusted-source integrity checks also defensible.
CPU W^X configuration is platform/OS-level hardening; closest hub is OS security despite hardware angle.
Manipulating input format/encoding to subvert processing; fits injection protection's input-handling scope, with HTTP input whitelisting as an alternative.
Poisoning RAG-indexed content is manipulation of augmentation data; the embedded prompt-injection payload makes indirect prompt injection a defensible secondary.
Persistent cookies holding sensitive data is sensitive data stored in browser-accessible client storage; protect-and-clear-cached-data is a plausible alternative reading.
Differential privacy applied to training data is explicitly named under training data obfuscation.
Device lock after inactivity is functionally a hard session timeout; OS security is a defensible alternative given OS-level implementation.
Session hijacking is fundamentally about session integrity; token entropy/algorithm hubs address only the prediction vector.
Reconnaissance via process enumeration is information disclosure, but the taxonomy's disclosure hubs are HTTP/debug oriented; no clean leaf home.
Encoding-bypass of validation is an injection-enabler; unstructured-data sanitization explicitly mentions encoding bypass and is a reasonable alternative.
Attack technique for finding sensitive local data; nearest defensive concept is minimizing sensitive data scattering, with encryption at rest as a mitigation alternative.
Modifying OS services maps loosely to OS security configuration; change management is a plausible process-side reading.
Section spans reconstruction, membership inference, and model extraction; inversion/membership inference is the core, with model exfiltration also covered.
White-box reverse engineering of software has no dedicated hub; nearest concept is preventing disclosure of implementation detail.
Covers direct modification, federated update poisoning, and supply-chain poisoning; parent hub best captures the breadth.
Supply chain risk management policy/procedures sits under supply chain management; policy review and compliance are weaker alternatives.
Mining information repositories is fundamentally a data access control failure; no leaf hub directly addresses repository data mining.
Incomplete deletion leaving data for new tenants is a data retention/remnant problem; decommissioning sanitization is a defensible alternative.
Availability-oriented poisoning of training data, including label flipping, is squarely data poisoning of training data.
Described by CAPEC itself as a CSRF variant riding the victim's session, differing mainly in harvesting data rather than performing an action.
Guardrails/moderator systems filtering model I/O map directly to Automated AI oversight, which explicitly names guardrails and output filtering.

Attack on OS-generated transient screenshots of sensitive data; nearest concept is protecting/clearing cached sensitive data, though the taxonomy has no exact home for OS-level screen capture leakage.
Input validation to reject oversized/malicious content causing AI resource exhaustion.
AI BOM is fundamentally a component/artifact inventory (SBOM analogue); AI-specific supply chain hubs are defensible alternatives.
Governance-level SCRM plan; Supply chain management is the only fitting branch though it lacks a leaf for SCRM planning.
Section covers indirect prompt injection mitigations, but the titled control (LLM moderator, output filtering, RLHF-based detection) matches automated oversight's moderator/guardrail systems.

Risk entry spanning third-party models, data, and deployment platforms; model supply chain management is the best control-side home, with data supply chain and supply-chain poisoning threat hub defensible.
Hardware debug interface chaining flaw; taxonomy has no hardware/debug hub, so design-level architecture is the least-bad fit.
Identifier lifecycle management (assignment, uniqueness, reuse prevention) has no precise hub; secure user management is the closest branch.
Logging/monitoring of AI model inputs, outputs, and agent behavior at runtime is inference monitoring.
Alternate-encoding bypass of validation is fundamentally an encoding/parsing consistency problem; general injection protection is a defensible alternative.
Organizational supply chain processes and controls; fits the Supply chain management branch though it is an intermediate hub.
Technique spans weight manipulation, poisoned data, and fine-tuning interference, so the AI model poisoning parent fits better than any single child.
